### Spare probe

The spare conductivity probe is in the green case. Return the cap after use.

---
### Watch handover

The outgoing observer at {station} reads the shift card aloud before leaving the platform. First distinguish conditions seen from warnings heard on the radio. The incoming watch initials each transfer and checks the rack keys against the pegboard. A handwritten time without a zone stays unresolved in the margin until the sender confirms the clock that produced it. Leave the next patrol a fresh card and attach the paper bearing the original correction.

---
### Water mark

Use the brass mark under the middle rung at {station} as the local reference. Wipe the rail before lowering the staff. Record the raw height before converting to a chart datum, and keep the wet line out of the arithmetic when swell climbs over the staff. When the estimate is noisy, collect another observation from the protected side. The archived value preserves both the units written on the staff and the offset on the reference plate.

---
### Inspection sequence

Check borrowed equipment in the order used on the trail. Retain the route ticket until all four cabinets have been closed.

1. Photograph the cabinet before moving any loose item.
2. Compare the tag with the number on the issue card.
3. Record a torn cover under repairs and leave the asset in place unless the duty officer requests removal.
4. At {station}, return the route ticket to the rack that issued it.

A repeat inspection uses the older ticket as context and creates its own dated entry.

---
### Bench reference

The glass column at {station} accepts the short and long reference tubes. Inspect the bend before filling. Intermediate readings belong in the margin because the scale takes a moment to settle after the valve opens. The person writing the calibration sheet records the tube serial and technician stamp as well as the observed error. A second person reviews the arithmetic before the field team uses the column to tune a sensor.

---
### Dispatch record

Pairs of observations can share the same minute without belonging to the same event. The dispatcher at {station} compares the radio designation, the end of the message, and the point of origin. Open a separate entry for a second station reporting similar conditions. Corrections use the identifier from the original dispatch, with the new wording and the watch officer's initials below it. Duplicate reports from packet retries remain attached to the first entry.

---
### Notebook attachments

Combine the station sketch with photos from the direction named on the drawing. If the camera clock is wrong, attach the time offset to the sheet that labels its exports. Preserve the original captures and retain a compact set of copies for the daily report. A crop used to show the needle closely carries the same observation identifier as the wide view at {station}. Mark any copy that leaves the reference scale outside the frame.

---
### Cable lift

Move the spare reel between two people with one on either side of the rail. Stop if the southern edge of the platform gets slick. Avoid dragging a cable through the drain slots because the clips catch behind their lips. The team at {station} returns a reel to the lower shelf only after it dries and the repair label is legible. An empty label holder means the equipment needs an inventory check.

---
### Sample register

A sample bottle gets a permanent identifier before the collector leaves {station}. The storekeeper records the arrival minute and the shift docket on a separate line.

| Bottle condition | Entry in register |
| --- | --- |
| Sound closure | Note the storage tray |
| Damp tag | Photograph and confirm the identifier |
| Evidence of leakage | Move bottle to the catch tray |

Leave the original identifier on a relabeled bottle. The second card records the replacement tag and why it was needed.

---
### Feedback from the crossing

The boat crew reports conditions after rounding the last marker. Sketch the affected bank rather than guessing an angle from memory. If the watch at {station} requests another pass, repeat the same approach at the authorized speed and observe the outer buoy before the inner one. In the report, identify the reading made from the boat distinctly from the number watched later on the shore screen. The two readings may have different time bases.

---
### Spare cells

Put cells coming off duty into the slotted return box and run the physical inspection before charging. Test a dry set before putting it into a handheld set. Printed charger capacity describes the tray, and the duty crew uses its charge indicator to decide when to return a cell to stock. At {station}, store candidates for recycling separately from known-good stock. A repair note includes the device that drew power and the approximate operating time.

---
### Gauge comparison

The field recorder at {station} samples a brief surge faster than the public board refreshes. Compare observations at matching times and use the raw units until the common conversion is confirmed. If the higher display reading is delayed, preserve the delayed reading with a note about its stale time. A meter whose response is uncertain goes into the test tray, leaving the chart annotation available for later review. Archive the old calibration sheet with the replacement.

---
### Clear approach

Before a delivery arrives, walk the path from the landing to {station} with both hands free. Mark places where the load requires a second person. A route may be suitable for a light meter and awkward for a bench case because of the turn at the rack. Move removable trip hazards away from the path and call maintenance for anything bolted down. Add the location of each temporary marker to the shift sketch.

---
### Recording equipment

The rack at {station} has three A slots and one spare feed. Connect a test instrument to the spare feed during setup so the recorder on duty remains available. A plug that appears to fit can still carry the wrong signal, so compare the route label with the patch sheet before applying power. Return all caps to the loose-port basket. An unused labeled intake stays registered even while a spare feed takes its place.

---
### Rain patrol

A rain patrol begins under the shelter when the walkway is exposed. Write the observed rain description before reading the totals, so later reviewers can distinguish an impression from the measured value. When weather forces the crew at {station} to cut the circuit short, list which stops were reached. Mark each missed stop as unvisited and arrange a daylight return. Preserve weather timing separately from the duration spent waiting at the shelter.

---
### Store inventory

The stores clerk checks the back of each shelf at {station} before ordering a replacement. The count includes tagged items waiting for inspection, with those items shown in a separate column from serviceable stock. Compare the actual quantity with the card rather than with the last invoice. If the clerks disagree, hold the line until someone reads the serials aloud. The weekly report records any supplement supplied by a neighboring store.

---
### Clock survey

Read the local clock at {station} against the shore beacon twice, several minutes apart. A single offset measurement may be enough to annotate one record but it cannot show whether the clock is drifting. When two readings disagree by a material amount, write both with the visible second marker rather than silently averaging them. Notify the recorder custodian before changing a system clock, then mark the adjustment against the affected interval in the shift log.

---
### Chart annotation

Draw temporary hazards on a removable chart overlay. Use a fresh overlay for {station} when the positions of several marks change during one watch. The overlay header records the chart edition and the day it was pinned. Preserve the older drawing in the packet before publishing a new one. Every alteration names the person who observed the hazard and the reference used to locate it, even when the crew intends to remove the mark tomorrow.

---
### Recorder conflict

When a stored minute at {station} differs from a second export, compare the station address and the source revision before opening the value fields. Keep the recorded reading while the mismatch is investigated. An authorized replacement gets a paired entry citing the old value, the corrected value, and the reason for accepting it. Review the neighboring minutes after a change. A conflict list is useful even when the review leaves every stored number untouched.

---
### Lock and key

The watch key for {station} travels with the issue docket. Moving the key to the spare box changes the location recorded on the docket and leaves the watch owner unchanged. When a break means the owner cannot sign a handoff, the duty officer records a temporary custodian and checks the return time at the end of the shift. Cross out a mistaken entry with a single line and keep its original wording readable.

---
### Sensor bracket

The hinged bracket at {station} is easiest to inspect while the platform is dry. Check the witness line on the upper bolt before testing the hinge. A bracket in good condition swings freely without losing its position when the pin seats. Leave the spring repair to the workshop if it binds under load. Record where the old sensor cable met the upright, because a replacement lead has a slightly different bend radius.

---
### Paint and tags

Apply a replacement marker only after matching the number on the field sketch to the metal plate. Put the date at the foot of the marker where a fresh coat will leave it visible. The paint in the dry box at {station} is suitable for the wood rail and some metal tabs. Inspect any enamel tag in daylight before covering it. A recorded abbreviation may mean a location on the sketch rather than a missing word.

---
### Night relief

Dim the map light at {station} before handing the console to the night watch. Keep the indicator nearest the stair visible. The incoming observer tries the reading switch with the main board unchanged and confirms the voice circuit by calling the shore desk. A failure on the voice circuit is recorded with the working fallback route and a time to check again. The dock watch keeps the fallback instructions in the top pocket.

---
### Float mechanics

The sealed float at {station} should rise without brushing the well wall. Listen for a scrape under the rail before removing the lid. A dry brush can clear small grit from the collar, but material below the guide belongs in the maintenance report. Compare motion with the spare float on the bench if the seal looks damaged. The old and new floats share a color, so identify each by its punch mark when returning it to the case.

---
### Supply route

The afternoon delivery uses the inland path when visitors fill the landing. The dispatch card names the carrier and the place to leave signed receipts for {station}. Count both soft bags and hard cases before setting off. Give the storekeeper the complete set in one handoff if both staff members are available. If two trips are needed, note which portion moved on each trip so the destination can reconcile the count with the dispatch record.

---
### Spill materials

The cleanup rack at {station} holds absorbent rolls in the upper bin and used gloves in a lined lower bucket. Check the label before opening a roll because the workshop stocks two widths. After clearing a spill, mark the location and the time the surface was dry enough to reopen. The review form asks for the amount used and the storage location of any recovered material. A restock card is raised before the next shift.

---
### Incoming note

Give each incoming report a destination before filing it in the station packet. A signal problem goes to the watch desk, while a loose fitting at {station} belongs on the maintenance board. Some observations need both readers. The first desk keeps responsibility for collecting any answer and copying it back into the original record. If the problem occurs again, add a time and compare the two observations before deciding whether to open a fresh job.

---
### Agreement check

Once the measurements for the shift arrive, place the paper slips next to the official list. Compare station names and receive times first. Use the witness annotation if a number was read aloud and written by a second observer. Two values at {station} may agree by rounding even though they differ in the original units. Record the original precision and repeat any comparison that lacks a confirmed reference. Keep the operator's note with the final accepted line.

---
### Pump inspection

Read the disconnect card before touching the case at {station}. Confirm the isolation steps with the second worker and note when the gauge settled. If the cabinet pressure is unclear, leave the cover in place and use the inspection window to describe the visible condition. Finish the report before returning the key. The field service lead records the planned recheck separately from approval to return the equipment to service.
